previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Ms. ___ was admitted with worsening shortness of breath, productive cough, and fever following recent bilateral toe amputations for dry gangrene. Initially treated for possible pneumonia, she was found to have Influenza A and was started on oseltamivir. Her asthma exacerbated by the flu was managed with increased prednisone and nebulizers, with gradual tapering as symptoms improved. Antibiotics were discontinued due to lack of evidence for bacterial pneumonia. She was stabilized on the medical floor, weaned off oxygen, and her leukocytosis and hyponatremia improved. Hypertension was managed with the addition of amlodipine. She was discharged home with home health services, on a short prednisone taper, new antihypertensive, and instructions to take an extra dose of furosemide to address mild fluid overload. Follow-up was arranged for lab monitoring and vascular surgery.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo F with a PMHx of asthma, COPD, SCC of the lung s/p  
resection (___), SCC of the throat s/p chemo/radiation, atrial  
fibrillation, and chronic pain syndrome (on chronic steroids and 
opiates) presenting with flare of chronic lung disease and 
hemorrhoidal bleeding.

# Shortness of breath: The patient was recently hospitalized for 
influenza and a COPD/asthma exacerbation. She was treated with 
Tamiflu, nebulizers and a steroid taper. On this admission she 
presented with severe course breath sounds, rhonchi and 
subjective dyspnea. She reported symptoms somewhat suggestive of 
a URI. The patient was treated with nebs, steroids and 
azithromycin for an exacerbation of her lung disease which 
includes asthma, COPD and bronchomalacia (from radiation). Her 
peak flow in the ED was 125 which improved to 225 with nebs and 
steroids. No consolidation was seen on CXR. Induced sputum was 
sent for culture, PCP, and acid fast testing; results were 
non-diagnostic. A CT of the chest revealed: mild progression of 
faint ground-glass opacities in the left upper lobe with 
otherwise stable ground glass opacities in the remaining left 
lung which could represent residual of recent infection, as the 
opacities on prior exam suggested underlying pneumonia. The 
patient underwent a bronchoscopy with BAL which revealed 
atypical squamous cells and abundant yeast. No pathologic 
organisms were identified. A significant amount of mucous 
plugging was found on bronchoscopy and relieved. She was started 
on mucolytics and given respiratory therapy. Her ambulatory 02 
sat was noted to dip only to the low ___ and recovered to the 
mid to high ___ with rest. She was never hypoxic at rest. The 
patient was started on Bactrim for PCP prophylaxis given her 
extensive/prolonged prednisone use. Immunoglobulins were checked 
given her recurrent infections. IgG returned low. The patient 
was given 20g of IVIg and tolerated the infusion well. She may 
have CVID as an explanation for her recurrent infections and 
history of low IgGs. She would have repeat Ig levels as an 
outpatient.  

# BRBPR: The patient's history and results of anoscopy in ED 
were consistent with a hemorrhoidal bleed. The patient's 
hematocrit was monitored with no significant fluctuations.  

# HTN: The patient was continued on amlodipine and carvedilol. 
Due to mild hypertension (SBPs 150s) lisinopril was initiated. 
The patient developed significant renal failure from the ACEi 
and it was discontinued. Addition of a thiazide diuretic may be 
necessary if the patient remains significantly hypertensive 
after restarting her furosemide.
 
# Dry Gangrene/PVD: S/p 6 toe amputations during a 
hospitalization in ___. The patient has routine follow up 
with the vascular center. Wound checks were conducted and 
dressing changed daily.

# Diastolic HF: The patient has a preserved EF on an 
echocardiogram from ___.  She was continued on carvedilol. 
Furosemide was briefly held during an episode of acute renal 
failure and subsequently restarted prior to discharge.

# Atrial fibrillation: The patient developed atrial fibrillation 
during a hospitalization in ___ with multifocal pneumonia. 
She is followed by cardiology as an outpatient. During the 
majority of her hospitalization she was in normal sinus rhythm. 
CHADS-2 score is 2; she is allergic to aspirin so therefore 
takes Plavix.  Carvedilol and amiodarone were continued. The 
patient QTc was monitored with the addition of azithromycin.

# CKD: The patient has stage III-IV CKD. Her baseline Cr is 
1.4-1.7. Her creatinine transiently increased when she was 
started on Bactrim and lisinopril. At discharge her creatinine 
was 1.7.

# Chronic Pain: The patient routinely endorses pain all over.Her 
pain is secondary to osteoarthritis and RA. She is on chronic 
steroids and opiates.  She was continued on home pain regimen 
with no adjustments made.
